r: A foggy morning by the Pacific Ocean here by the beach in Long Beach, California. And 25 of the world’s best Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME Duelists have come to decide who will be crowned as the 2010 World Champion!
Here are the Top 8 finalists after 5 rounds of Swiss Pair play today. These 8 finalists will compete tomorrow for the title of 2010 Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME World Champion!

1. Kei Kuwano (Japan – 13 points)
2. Hideki Kawai (Japan – 13 points)
3. Aaron Noel (Canada – 12 points)

8. Stefano Sluis (Netherlands – 9 points)
It’s Day 2 at the 2010 Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME World Championship, and the Top 8 has just started. Here’s the list of who’s playing against whom, and who’s running what:

Table 1
Kei Kuwano (Japan – Herald of Perfection) vs. Stefano Sluis (Netherlands – Infernity)
Kei Kuwano (Japan – Herald of Perfection) wins and advances to the Semi-Finals

Table 2
Hideki Kawai (Japan – Frog Monarch) vs. Tae Woo Kim (South Korea – Blackwings)
Tae Woo Kim (South Korea – Blackwings) wins and advances to the Semi-Finals

Table 3
Aaron Noel (Canada – Blackwings) vs. Vincent Paglia (USA – Blackwings)
Vincent Paglia (USA – Blackwings) wins and advances to the Semi-Finals
Table 4

(Taiwan – Frog Monarch) vs. Galileo De Obaldia (Panama – Frog OTK)
Galileo De Obaldia (Panama – Frog OTK) wins and advances to the Semi-Finals
The Semi-Finals for the 2010 World Championship have begun!

At one table:
Kei Kuwano (Japan – Herald of Perfection) vs. Galileo De Obaldia (Panama – Frog OTK)
Galileo De Obaldia (Panama – Frog OTK) wins and advances to the Final Round

At the other table:
Vincent Paglia (USA – Blackwings) vs. Tae Woo Kim (South Korea – Blackwings)
Vincent Paglia (USA – Blackwings) wins and advances to the Final Round

Each of these competitors will win a beautiful glass trophy with a globe and an etched 3D Stardust Dragon sculpted within. Each trophy also contains their prize card for this event. The ultimate winner will receive
– one of 2 copies of that card that will be released (the other will go to the winner of the video game championship). Second, third, and fourth place will receive
(six copies total of this card will be released – 3 for the Trading Card Game and 3 for the video game finalists).
All that remains to be decided is which competitor will receive which trophy and which prize card, plus the fame of being crowned 2010 World Champion!
In the 3rd/4th place final match, Kei Kuwano of Japan, playing his Herald of Perfection Deck, has defeated Tae Woo Kim of South Korea, playing Blackwings.
The final match will be held later today, between Vincent Paglia of the United States, playing Blackwings, and Galileo De Obaldia from Panama, playing his Frog OTK Deck.

In the finals of this year’s World Championship event, Blackwing Duelist Vincent Paglia from the USA faced off against Frog OTK Duelist Galileo De Obaldia from Panama.
